title: The Welly Walk
strapline: Boots on, off we go — a wandering walk beyond the gate to notice, collect and wonder at the world nearby.
intent: Children come to know their local patch as learners — the park, the trees, the shops, the people who help us.
Children practise slow, curious noticing on foot — the seasons changing, a snail on the wall, a puddle, a passing bus.
Children build stamina, balance and coordination walking over varied ground, up kerbs and across grass.
Children learn real-world awareness and simple road and outdoor safety on genuine journeys.
Children gather natural treasures and questions to bring back and explore further.
implementation: Keep the destination loose — the walk itself is the point; follow the children's noticing rather than marching to a target.
Go often and in all seasons and weathers, so children track the same route changing through the year.
Slow right down to their pace: stop for the snail, the puddle, the interesting gate — the wonder is in the small things.
Carry collecting bags and a magnifier, and gather leaves, conkers and treasures to investigate back at the setting.
Weave in safety naturally — holding on near roads, stopping at the kerb, looking and listening — as real, purposeful learning.
Talk all the way — name what you see, wonder aloud, count the red doors — turning the walk into a river of language.
key_questions: What can you notice that's changed since last time?
What treasure have you found to bring back?
Who are the people who help us that we can see?
What can you hear on our walk today?
How do we keep safe when we cross near the road?

impact.text: Children know their local patch as learners — the park, the shops, the people who help us.
Children notice the world on outings — wind, leaves, buses, seasons — and want to explore it.
Children talk about what they see and find on local walks and collect treasures.
Children walk, balance and negotiate varied ground and obstacles with growing control.
Children ask real questions about the world around them and expect real answers.

enhancements: A seasonal photo of the same tree or corner each visit, building a year-long record of change.
A collecting bag and a 'treasure table' back at base to sort and examine the finds.
A simple picture map of the route children help make and follow.
A listening-and-spotting card — tick off the bird, the bus, the postbox, the puddle.
A visit with purpose — posting a letter, choosing fruit at the shop — meeting the people who help us.

playing_exploring: Children explore the world beyond the gate with open, unhurried curiosity.
Collecting treasures and noticing small things invites hands-on investigation.
active_learning: Children walk further and notice more over repeated walks, building stamina and attention.
Their own discoveries drive the walk, sustaining engagement journey after journey.
creating_thinking: Children notice change and pattern in the seasons and their local world and ask why.
They make connections between the setting and the community it sits in.
